input.title: Fix token lifetime parsing in configuration
input.body:
File: src/config.ts

Change the token TTL parsing to support duration strings instead of misinterpreting them as integers, or validate the input to reject non-integer minutes strings. This fixes the issue of short token lifetimes caused by strings like '12h' being parsed as 12.

input.title: Add report name filter to reports list endpoint
input.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

Implement a name filter query parameter on the reports list endpoint to allow searching reports by their name, enabling easier location of saved reports by name.

input.title: Fix language preference to respect Accept-Language quality values
input.body:
File: src/i18n/index.ts

Update the language selection logic to respect the quality (q) values from the Accept-Language header, so clients preferring French by a higher q value get French responses.

input.body:
label: bug
file: src/config.ts

The configuration code interprets the TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES environment variable strictly as an integer number of minutes, so values like '12h' are parsed as 12 instead of 720. This causes tokens to expire much sooner than expected. The fix is to validate or parse the input properly to prevent this confusion.

label: question
file: none

The health check endpoint returns HTTP 200 but reports a "degraded" status in the JSON body. The current behavior is by design: the HTTP status shows service availability, whereas the "degraded" status signals partial issues. The reporter should decide how the load balancer's probe treats this. No code change is needed.

label: feature
file: src/api/reports.ts

This adds a search name filter to the reports list endpoint, enabling users to find saved reports by name instead of paging through many pages. The change is mostly in the API reports router to add an optional name filter to the list query.

label: docs
file: src/api/auth.ts

The password validation rules are described by the min and max length constraints in the password-reset confirm schema in src/api/auth.ts, where passwords must be between 10 and 200 characters. Adding this information to the API reference or help desk documentation will clarify the rules for end users.

label: bug
file: src/i18n/index.ts

The current Accept-Language header parsing picks the first supported language ignoring the q quality weights. The fix is to enhance the language selection to respect these quality values, so clients preferring French by q get French responses correctly.
